title: Territory — Editor Intro
summary: Editorial opening splash: morning comes after the household's first night in 5B, but Gunnar still lacks the most basic orientation he trusts; clouds hide the sky while the exterior iron continues upward.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, cloudy early morning
panelPlan: Full-page editorial/title splash with no conventional grid. Inside sparse apartment 5B in gray early-morning light: the brass key hangs near the door, the drafty window shows a blank overcast sky, and Gunnar stands looking upward along the exterior iron beyond the glass.
Keep the room materially simple and newly occupied. Do not show a usable map, readable contact card, phone knowledge, or other modern navigation tools.
The eye should travel from the locked room to the exterior iron and finally to the clouded sky above the building.
Integrate the captions as deliberate editorial typography with strong hierarchy. End with Welcome to TERRITORY.

title: Tomorrow Is Not Tonight
summary: Gunnar uses the exterior iron to reach higher ground on the first morning, taking Carrie's overnight restriction literally rather than understanding a broader building rule.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B and exterior fire escape, early morning
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn wakes to the sound of the rear window opening. Gunnar is already stepping carefully onto the exterior iron.
Medium: Bjorn remains inside while Gunnar looks upward toward the next landing and roofline.
Two-shot across the open window: Bjorn recalls Carrie's restriction from the night before.
Wide exterior: Gunnar begins climbing upward through the gray morning while Bjorn watches from 5B.

dialogueInline.text: Carrie said not to climb outside.
That is why I am going.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: A Man on the Roof
summary: Gunnar reaches the cloudy roof and meets Silas for the first time; Silas treats him as a new neighbor while making it clear that unusual activity on the roof will not go unnoticed.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar reaches the flat roof and finds only gray cloud, water towers, brick walls, antennas and neighboring rooftops. The sun is completely hidden.
Medium: He studies the cloud cover and horizon, dissatisfied; nothing in the sky gives him the fixed point he came for.
Wide: Silas appears from the opposite side of the roof with coffee, notices Gunnar and slows.
Two-shot: Silas keeps a neighborly distance. His tone is casual, but his curiosity is real.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. Don't screw up. I'm keeping my eye on you.
I am also keeping my eye on you.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: The Black Glass Has an Opinion
summary: Silas offers a phone compass, but Gunnar does not treat an unfamiliar device as knowledge; with the sun hidden, north remains unresolved.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan: Medium: Silas notices Gunnar repeatedly checking the blank sky and asks what he is looking for.
Close: Silas takes out his phone and shows the compass screen, with the display visible only as a simple directional interface rather than readable technical detail.
Medium: Gunnar studies the device itself rather than accepting the indicated direction.
Wide: Gunnar looks back to the clouds and surrounding roofline; the phone has not solved the problem for him.

dialogueInline.text: Does the glass tell you where north is?
That's as much as I know.
The sky will tell me when it returns.
Are you planning to wait here?

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: No North Yet
summary: Gunnar returns without orientation, but his description of the roof gives Bjorn a different idea: open sky offers somewhere for smoke to go.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar climbs back through the rear window into 5B. Bjorn is awake; Astrid and the two Kin continue quiet morning tasks in the background without speaking.
Two-shot: Bjorn expects an answer about north and gets weather instead.
Medium: Gunnar describes the roof physically—open above, wind moving across it, no beams or ceiling to hold smoke.
Close on Bjorn as that last observation becomes useful for a different unresolved problem.

dialogueInline.text: The roof is open above. Wind crosses it.
Not as it does in the room.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: The Follow-Up
summary: Carrie arrives because the previous night's fire-escape incident is already in the DTI file and immediately discovers that Gunnar has used the exterior route again—after the literal end of her overnight prohibition.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie enters 5B with her folder while the household is awake and active. The recovered snare cord remains bundled with Second Male Kin's gear.
Medium: she notices Gunnar's damp boots and the open rear window before he closes it.
Two-shot: Gunnar states where he went without embarrassment.
Three-shot Carrie/Bjorn/Gunnar: Bjorn supplies the literal timing distinction from the previous night.
Close on Carrie as she looks at the existing DTI follow-up notice in her folder, then at the window.

dialogueInline.text: I told you not to climb outside.
The pigeon is already in your file. Do not give me today's problem before breakfast.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: First Fire
summary: Bjorn and Gunnar act on the roof's obvious advantage for smoke; the silent Kin begin assembling a hearth base from loose rooftop metal until Carrie stops the project on the simplest possible ground: the material is not theirs.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie follows Bjorn and Gunnar onto the roof and finds First Male Kin and Second Male Kin silently moving loose sheet-metal pieces from a maintenance stack toward a clear roof area.
Medium: Gunnar has selected a location with open sky and moving air; Bjorn is judging the surface and spacing rather than improvising recklessly.
Fast medium: Carrie reaches the loose metal before any fire is built.
Medium: the Kin stop immediately and wait; nobody argues that dangerous work should continue.
Wide: the metal begins going back exactly where it came from.

dialogueInline.text: Then we will use something else.
There will be no fire on the roof.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: Winter Is Not Today
summary: Carrie finally hears the practical need beneath the hearth project: Bjorn is not cold now; he is unwilling to enter winter with only one source of warmth that nobody in the household understands or controls.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan: Medium: the Kin silently return the last loose metal while Carrie stays with Bjorn and Gunnar.
Two-shot Carrie/Bjorn: she asks why a spring morning has become a hearth problem.
Medium on Gunnar: he points only toward the building below, not to any system diagram or named equipment.
Close on Bjorn: his concern is redundancy and responsibility, not fear of modern technology.
Wide: Carrie remains unconvinced by the solution even though the need itself is clearer.

dialogueInline.text: Why do you need a hearth in April?
We do not need it today.
Then why are we doing this today?
Because winter does not wait until you are cold to begin preparing.
The room becomes warm. We do not know how.
If it stops, we have no second fire.
Keeping the room warm is the landlord's responsibility.
And being cold would be ours.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Something That Is Ours
summary: The household solves the ownership objection without abandoning the fire plan: Bjorn and Gunnar bring their own heavy cooking pot upstairs as a contained vessel while Astrid and the Kin remain present but silent.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B and roof stair, midday
panelPlan: Wide: back in 5B, Bjorn and Gunnar inspect the household's own heavy iron cooking pot while Astrid watches from the food area and the Kin continue other tasks without speaking.
Medium: Gunnar checks the pot's stability and depth; this is practical firecraft, not discovery of fire.
Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar carry the pot upward together while one Kin silently brings a bucket of water.
Final panel: the pot reaches the roof. The building-owned metal remains untouched in the background.
source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Second Fire
summary: Bjorn and Gunnar light a small, physically competent test fire in their own iron pot; Silas sees it, fulfilling his promise to watch the roof.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, early afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: the heavy iron pot sits on a bare masonry service area well clear of roof clutter. A water bucket is within reach; the Kin stand back and remain silent.
Medium: Gunnar checks the wind and Bjorn checks the pot's stability before lighting a very small test fire.
Insert: a controlled flame takes. Nobody treats the flame as a novelty.
Wide: Silas appears at the far side of the roof and stops when he sees smoke.
Two-shot Silas/Gunnar across the roof: Silas takes out his phone.

dialogueInline.text: Wind is moving away from the building.
So that's what the pot was for.
Carrie is going to love this.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Out
summary: Carrie arrives before the test becomes a larger fire; she does not teach fire safety, because that is not the problem. The problem is that another rooftop incident can jeopardize the placement.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, early afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie reaches the roof quickly and sees the small contained fire, water bucket and silent Kin standing clear.
Medium: Bjorn is ready to defend the setup's physical competence; Carrie does not debate it.
Close: Carrie gives one direct command. Gunnar immediately covers or extinguishes the small fire safely.
Medium: Carrie points to the building below, making the housing consequence the issue rather than explaining combustion.
Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar carry the still-warm pot back toward the stairs.

dialogueInline.text: Yesterday was a pigeon on the fire escape. Today cannot become a roof fire.
The placement can be endangered without anyone burning.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: The Wrong Danger
summary: After Carrie leaves, Bjorn and Gunnar understand exactly enough of the institutional consequence to become more determined: the next fire must create no complaint and no new case problem.
settingText: Bushwick apartment stair and 5B, afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar carry the iron pot back into 5B. The Kin follow silently with the water bucket.
Medium: Bjorn sets the pot down; it cannot remain upstairs because Astrid needs it for food.
Two-shot: Gunnar separates the physical danger from the housing danger Carrie actually named.
Close on Bjorn: instead of abandoning the idea, he converts the restriction into a design requirement.
Wide: the household's own cooking pot returns to the food area, ending attempt two.

dialogueInline.text: The fire was not what she feared most.
Then the next fire makes trouble for no one.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Ask the Merchant
summary: Bjorn and Gunnar solve the dedicated-material problem by asking the bodega owner for unwanted iron; he gives them a damaged lidded stockpot while making clear that whatever follows is their business.
settingText: Bushwick bodega, afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar return to the familiar corner bodega without Carrie. The owner recognizes them and keeps working.
Medium: Bjorn asks for iron the merchant no longer wants rather than trying to buy a modern specialty object.
Close: the owner studies both men before pulling a dented heavy stockpot with a damaged handle and matching lid from behind the counter or storage area.
Medium: Gunnar checks the vessel physically; it is thick, stable and no longer useful to the merchant for normal kitchen work.
Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar leave carrying the pot while the owner watches them go.

dialogueInline.text: Do you have iron you do not want?
I have a pot with a broken handle.
Take the pot. Leave my name out of whatever happens next.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Third Attempt
summary: The third hearth is deliberately built from their own dedicated material and their own fire knowledge; they wait on wind and placement rather than treating Carrie's objection as a challenge to safety.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late afternoon under lingering clouds
panelPlan: Wide: the dented lidded stockpot has become the core of a compact contained stove on a bare masonry service pad, with no building material removed or altered. Astrid and the two Kin are present but silent.
Medium: Gunnar checks the surrounding clearance and wind while Bjorn tests the lid and stability.
Insert: a full bucket of water is placed within easy reach.
Medium: the wind shifts toward the building. Gunnar stops the lighting attempt before Bjorn reaches for fuel.
Wide: everyone simply waits. Competence is shown through restraint.

title: Third Fire
summary: When the wind settles, the household lights the dedicated contained stove; the third attempt has solved ownership, physical control and immediate nuisance without resolving whether Carrie will accept it.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, early evening
panelPlan: Wide: the wind has eased. Bjorn lights a modest fire inside the dedicated lidded metal stove; the household gathers around it without crowding the clear zone.
Medium: Astrid and the Kin use the warmth quietly; nobody treats the fire as entertainment or spectacle.
Insert: thin smoke rises cleanly into the open air; water and lid remain within reach.
Wide: Silas appears and watches from a distance, phone still in his pocket this time.
Two-shot Silas/Gunnar: the fire is obviously deliberate and controlled, but still unmistakably a rooftop fire.

dialogueInline.text: I'm still deciding whether that helps.

title: Still No North
summary: The third fire holds safely while Gunnar's original problem remains unresolved; the clouds are thinning but the stars have not yet appeared.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof at dusk
panelPlan: Wide: dusk darkens the roof while the contained fire remains small. The household occupies the space naturally; Astrid and the Kin remain silent.
Medium: Gunnar repeatedly looks away from the fire toward breaks forming in the cloud cover.
Two-shot: Silas recognizes what Gunnar is waiting for.
Close on Gunnar as the clouds still hide the useful stars.
Wide: the roof has become useful before it has become orienting.

dialogueInline.text: I can show you the phone again.

title: Carrie Comes Back
summary: Carrie returns to complete the required follow-up from the previous night's exterior-stair incident and finds that the entire household has established a third, much more competent rooftop fire.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B and roof access, evening
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie reaches 5B with her folder and finds the apartment occupied only by traces of recent activity; the household is above.
Medium: she follows the sound of movement upward and emerges onto the roof.

Large reveal: the whole household is gathered around the compact contained stove. The building-owned metal stack is untouched. Water, lid, clear space and restrained flame are visible without being presented as a checklist.
Close on Carrie: annoyance arrives first, then slows as she actually looks at how the household is using the fire.

dialogueInline.text: The merchant had no use for it.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: If You Require It
summary: Bjorn gives Carrie the choice she has been trying to force all day: he will extinguish the fire if she requires it, but he will not pretend the household's need for an independent hearth has disappeared.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, evening
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie walks once around the setup without touching it. She sees the household-owned vessel, modest flame, water, lid and clear masonry.
Two-shot Carrie/Bjorn: Bjorn does not argue that she must approve; he states what he will do if she orders it extinguished.
Wide: Astrid and the Kin remain near the warmth without speaking. Their presence makes the hearth's function obvious without anyone explaining it.
Close on Carrie holding the DTI folder she came to complete; she does not open it yet.

dialogueInline.text: If you require it out, I will put it out.
Tomorrow we will still need a second fire before winter.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: What It Is For
summary: Carrie watches the household use the hearth rather than debating it; the fire is plainly not rebellion or novelty but a piece of home they know how to maintain.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, evening
panelPlan: Quiet visual page. Carrie remains standing at first while the household continues around the contained fire without performing for her.

Astrid warms her hands briefly before returning to food preparation nearby; First Male Kin adjusts a chair; Second Male Kin brings one more piece of fuel and leaves it beside Bjorn rather than feeding it himself.
Gunnar checks the sky again. Bjorn checks the fire and lid. The actions are ordinary to them.
Carrie finally sits on a low dry surface at the edge of the group, still holding the unopened folder.
No dialogue. Do not caption Carrie's realization or explain the emotional beat.
source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

title: The Sky Opens
summary: After a full day of cloud, the evening sky begins to clear; Gunnar immediately leaves the fire's center to recover the orientation problem he never solved that morning.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, later evening
panelPlan: Wide: a break opens in the cloud cover above Bushwick, revealing the first clear stars.
Close on Gunnar noticing before anyone else.
Medium: he moves away from the fire to a darker edge of the roof with a broader view of the sky.
Wide from behind Gunnar: more cloud peels away, exposing enough of the northern sky for him to work from familiar stars.
Silas may be visible at a distance near his own access point, watching without interrupting.
